name: Intel Games Task Scheduler
listed_description: A task scheduling framework designed for the needs of game developers.
reason: README and documentation/pages markdown (developer guide, quick start, micro-scheduler and containers pages, features list) contain no benchmark numbers or comparison against TBB or any other baseline; the gts_malloc test page is a TBD stub; no benchmark directory (source/ holds gts/ and user_config.h). Repository archived by Intel on 2023-01-03 (last commit 2023-01-03). Intel's Games Task Scheduler article and the github.io docs were not reachable (ENOTFOUND www.intel.com).

name: itlib
listed_description: A collection of std-like single-header C++ libraries
reason: Only qualitative performance wording (pod_vector skips constructors and uses memcpy/realloc, flat_map cache locality). test/b-rand_dist.cpp (picobench, added 2025-10-31) compares itlib::uniform_int_distribution and fast_uniform_real_distribution with std::uniform_int_distribution and std::uniform_real_distribution, but the repo publishes no results: no numbers in README, header comments, test README or the two commit messages, and a WebSearch for published results found none. The benchmark could be run to produce numbers; none exist to cite.

name: junction
listed_description: A library of concurrent data structures in C++.
reason: Directional claim only in reachable material: the author's blog post (New Concurrent Hash Maps for C++, preshing.com 2016-02-01) says Junction's two fastest maps outperform all other concurrent maps on a Core i7-5930K, seen as a WebSearch snippet, no numbers. The repo README has no results; samples/MapScalabilityTests (TestAllMaps.py, RenderGraphs.py) builds the same test against Leapfrog, Linear, Grampa, TBB, folly, libcuckoo, libcds Michael map, nbds, tervel and std::map, so the benchmark is reproducible but no numbers are published in the repo. The blog (ENOTFOUND preshing.com) and the peer-reviewed comparison by Maier et al. (arXiv 1601.04017, benchmarks Junction Linear/Grampa/Leapfrog against tbb::concurrent_hash_map; ENOTFOUND arxiv.org) hold the likely numbers; retry from an environment that reaches them. A Hacker News commenter reported TBB scaling better than Junction past 6 cores, so the claim is not clear-cut.

name: Kangaru
listed_description: A dependency injection container for C++11 and C++14.
reason: README only says 'Low runtime overhead' and lists 'Even better performance (ongoing)' on its roadmap. benchmark/src/benchmarks.cpp (Google Benchmark) measures only kangaru itself (service_bench, emplace_bench, half-insert variants across 8 to 128 services); it includes no other DI container, no manual-construction baseline, and no results are published in the repo.

name: libcds
listed_description: A C++ library of Concurrent Data Structures.
reason: readme.md and change.log contain no benchmark numbers or comparison against TBB, Boost.Lockfree or std containers (only the line 'SplitList performance improving'). test/stress holds stress tests with no published results, and two WebSearch queries for libcds-versus-TBB or Boost.Lockfree comparisons found none. libcds appears only as a competitor (Michael map) inside Junction's scalability test script, with no numbers. Last commit 2022-03-01.
